reasoning: The document contains 3 major defects and 3 minor defects. The most significant issues are structural: a continuous table spanning two pages was split, with the second page converted to an improperly numbered list, and header/footer elements were erroneously retained in the output. Because there are 3 major defects (falling within the 1-5 range), this document requires HUMAN_REVIEW according to the routing rules.

concerns.analysis: The source document contains a continuous tabular structure that spans both pages. It begins on page 1 with column headers 'Tab', 'Topic', and 'Presenter', and continues with rows 1 through 6. The tabular alignment continues onto page 2 with rows 7 through 13. In the output JSON, page 1 is correctly extracted as a table, but the table breaks at the page boundary, and the continuation of the tabular data on page 2 (rows 7 through 13) is extracted as a list, completely losing the column structure.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 2 continuation of the table with aligned columns for item numbers (7-13), topics, and presenters.

concerns.analysis: Items 7 through 13 on page 2 represent a continuation of a numbered sequence from page 1. In the source, they are explicitly numbered '7.', '8.', etc. In the output JSON, they are placed in a new ordered list, and their explicit numbers have been stripped from the text. Because this ordered list does not have a start value and is not connected to items 1-6 (which were embedded in a table), the HTML rendering will restart numbering from 1 instead of 7, causing a renumbering defect.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: 7. Education Committee Report... 8. Funding Committee Report...
concerns.output_quote: {"text": "Education Committee Report...........................................Chuck Greene/Angie Turbeville"}, {"text": "Funding Committee Report..................................................David Bone/Marsha Tapler"}

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (1): NC 911 Board Agenda • Friday, May 22, 2020 • Page 1 of 2
concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=1. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

The source PDF applies specific text formatting for emphasis, notably italics on the phrase '(Roll Call Vote Required)'. The HTML output strips this italicization and renders it as plain text. Because the text still clearly states the requirement, this is evaluated as a minor loss of visual formatting.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 2 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=2, examples=['https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/19%3ameeting_MWQzY', 'tel:+1%20984-204-1487,,785259301#%20']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

concerns.description: Flattened sub-lists: 2 item(s) contain nested sub-items (a/b/c or bullets) as plain text instead of structured children
concerns.analysis: flattened_sublists=2. Examples: p1 table: a) Minutes of Previous Meetings – April , b) NG 911 Fund/Account, c) CMRS Fund/Account; p1 table: a) COVID-19 Update, b) SL 2020-3 (Section 4.38 Regulatory Fl, c) Upcoming Board Meetings. Sub-items embedded as newline-delimited text lose semantic nesting in HTML — screen readers can't navigate the hierarchy.

action_items: Reconstruct the table on page 2 to merge with the page 1 table and preserve rows 7-13.
Structure the flattened sub-lists (a/b/c) as proper nested lists within the table cells.
Move the standalone hyperlinks to be inline within their respective text.
Restore italic formatting to the '(Roll Call Vote Required)' text.
